scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9007: Hello IT, the partner connection keeps HICCUPING --
their machine drops out on me every so often and feels slow in between.
Something around the connection must be going wrong, but I don't know what.
Could someone look at it and make it stay up for more than five minutes!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  peering is stable and reachability is loss-free. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an intermittent/flap
  symptom that is not occurring -- does the agent check session stability and
  loss against the live network, or confabulate a flapping peering?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a flapping/slow peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2)
reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and stable low latency, the router1<->router2
eBGP session is Established with a steady uptime (not resetting), and no route
churn is observed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the peering is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent checks the BGP
session state/uptime on router1 and router2 and runs a sustained ping pc1->pc2,
finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the peering flapping or resetting router1/router2's BGP to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A full four-phase diagnostic pass found no fault mechanism consistent with the reported "hiccuping" connection. Phase A (infra_sweep, l2_snapshot) was clean: no ACL drop rules, no addressing anomalies, no static ARP entries, no genuine MAC conflicts. The L2 duplicate-MAC report covered only kernel tunnel interfaces (tunl0, gre0, etc.) present on every device with null MACs — baseline Linux behavior. Phase B showed both BGP sessions Established (AS1 ↔ AS2) with healthy keepalive exchange. The BGP neighbor detail showed 1 AS-PATH loop filtered on each side: each router re-advertises the learned prefix back to its single eBGP peer, and BGP's own loop detection correctly drops it — standard two-router eBGP behavior, not a fault. The last-reset reason on router1 was "connection collision" (both sides initiated simultaneously at startup) and on router2 "no path to neighbor before first connect" — both are normal initialization artifacts, not recurring faults. Connections established: 1, dropped: 0 on both routers, confirming no session flaps since startup. tc_snapshot found only default pfifo_fast qdiscs on all six interfaces — no shaping, rate-limiting, or delay injection. Phase D pressure_sweep found no stress tools, CPU spikes, or socket exhaustion. No BGP or daemon log entries existed. The ticket's symptom has no supporting mechanism or historical trace in the current lab state, so the claim is unconfirmed. Root cause: no anomaly is present; the topology is operating normally.
Fix: no corrective action required. If the complaint recurs, capture BGP neighbor uptime and BGP notification counters during an active drop event to confirm or rule out a hold-timer-expiry flap.
